import re
import os

# Find all .unwrap() in non-test code
for root, dirs, files in os.walk('src'):
    for f in files:
        if not f.endswith('.rs'):
            continue
        path = os.path.join(root, f)
        with open(path) as fh:
            content = fh.read()
        lines = content.split('\n')
        in_test = False
        brace_depth = 0
        test_brace_start = 0
        for i, line in enumerate(lines):
            stripped = line.strip()
            # Track #[cfg(test)] modules and #[test] functions
            if '#[cfg(test)]' in stripped or '#[test]' in stripped:
                in_test = True
                test_brace_start = brace_depth
            
            brace_depth += line.count('{') - line.count('}')
            
            if in_test and brace_depth <= test_brace_start:
                in_test = False
            
            if not in_test and '.unwrap()' in line:
                print(f'{path}:{i+1}: {line.strip()}')
"

input.command:
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Handle Ctrl+D as abort signal in prompts

The custom yes/no and dumb-terminal select prompts read keys
in a loop but did not handle Ctrl+D (byte 0x04). In raw mode
the console crate maps this to Key::Char('\x04'), which fell
through to the catch-all arm and was silently ignored—leaving
the user stuck in an infinite loop or triggering a panic
further up the call stack.

Detect Key::Char('\x04') as an abort signal in both
prompt_yes_no and prompt_select_dumb, returning an
UnexpectedEof IO error that callers propagate via `?`.
EOF
)"

commit 1245a2f9543f4ef571a1532340d7363093c13a22
Author: benchmark <benchmark@localhost>
Date:   Sat May 16 18:02:31 2026 -0600

    Handle Ctrl+D as abort signal in prompts
    
    The custom yes/no and dumb-terminal select prompts read keys
    in a loop but did not handle Ctrl+D (byte 0x04). In raw mode
    the console crate maps this to Key::Char('\x04'), which fell
    through to the catch-all arm and was silently ignored—leaving
    the user stuck in an infinite loop or triggering a panic
    further up the call stack.
    
    Detect Key::Char('\x04') as an abort signal in both
    prompt_yes_no and prompt_select_dumb, returning an
    UnexpectedEof IO error that callers propagate via `?`.

 src/ui/prompts.rs | 49 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 1 file changed, 49 insertions(+)

Handle Ctrl+D as abort signal in prompts

The custom yes/no and dumb-terminal select prompts read keys
in a loop but did not handle Ctrl+D (byte 0x04). In raw mode
the console crate maps this to Key::Char('\x04'), which fell
through to the catch-all arm and was silently ignored—leaving
the user stuck in an infinite loop or triggering a panic
further up the call stack.

Detect Key::Char('\x04') as an abort signal in both
prompt_yes_no and prompt_select_dumb, returning an
UnexpectedEof IO error that callers propagate via `?`.
EOF

Author: benchmark <benchmark@localhost>
Date:   Sat May 16 18:02:31 2026 -0600

    Handle Ctrl+D as abort signal in prompts
    
    The custom yes/no and dumb-terminal select prompts read keys
    in a loop but did not handle Ctrl+D (byte 0x04). In raw mode
    the console crate maps this to Key::Char('\x04'), which fell
    through to the catch-all arm and was silently ignored—leaving
    the user stuck in an infinite loop or triggering a panic
    further up the call stack.
    
    Detect Key::Char('\x04') as an abort signal in both
    prompt_yes_no and prompt_select_dumb, returning an
    UnexpectedEof IO error that callers propagate via `?`.
